section: Structural Support and Its Limits / Value-only evidence restores alternatives
manuscript_claim: \emph{Proof.} Map one canonical required fact to two aliases $u,v$. Both change from false to true. Either singleton establishes the final true value, but their intersection does not; complete evidence instead records both pairs. For hardness, reduce from set cover~[citation]: take a universe $U$ and sets $B_j$ whose union is $U$ (infeasible instances can be rejected before the reduction). Create one changed alias $a_j$ per set and one required canonical fact $c_e$ per element. Map $c_e$ to aliases whose sets contain $e$. Selecting changed aliases makes every $c_e$ true exactly when the corresponding sets cover $U$, preserving cardinality. \hfill$\square$
support_role: primary source for the set-cover hardness premise; the paper then gives its own cardinality-preserving mapping to value-only support
